gate1.note:
GATE 1 APPROVED - round 3. Human decision; the stopping rule was approve-eligible on its own (no --override).

RULE: 0 blocking findings, 7 worth a look, 0 blocking owned by 'nothing'. Linter 0 errors / 0 warnings. Sessions 40.0 / 37.0 against the cap, session 1 carries setup at 2 cuts against session 2's 3, E110 and E113 both pass. 11 criteria, 11 distinct tests, no test shared between two criteria. 5 cuts. gate1-check re-run independently of the workflow that produced it; spec-status, lint.json, ambiguity-meta.json and gate1.json all bound to spec hash 729cfc0b1ba5 with no drift.

WHAT ROUND 2'S REJECTION ASKED FOR IS DONE, AND WIDER: B1 was the unpinned cut-cell-cycle marker boundary. spec.md:188-200 now fixes where the closing marker goes for ALL FIVE cuts, not just that one, and records why it had to be pinned - invisible to cutter (balance and placement, not contents), to return-safety (no return), and to test-runner (only ever sees app/). Restated at :301 and :513. Round 2's W1, the closed rule not being total for clue = [], is also closed: :146 makes it total explicitly and :348-353 handles the degenerate line where clue and runsOf are both [].

ACCEPTED WITH EYES OPEN - four findings owned by 'nothing' ship as written:

  W4 - spec.md requires ep-puzzles-list entries to have 'no other key' but c-1-1
       grades only 'no solution key'. A Builder that spreads extra fields onto the
       derived puzzle passes and hands the browser the answer, defeating the
       property the derived-not-stored design exists to protect. WATCH AT GATE 2:
       read the puzzles-list response shape by hand, do not trust the green test.
  W1 - the clue-strip status rule is silent on the window between a click and its
       response. 'Keep the old value' and 'reset to open and repaint' both ship;
       the second makes every green line blink on every later click. Cosmetic, but
       it lands in the session-2 payoff. WATCH AT GATE 2 in the browser.
  W2 - the 'What nothing checks' section lists one constraint and reads as
       exhaustive; the out-of-order discard rule belongs in it and is missing.
  W3 - board-loading and the text of puzzle-title are declared and never graded.

  W5 (pack-writer) - session 2 budgeted to exactly 40 with no slack while carrying
       the largest cut. Do NOT fix by moving a cut into session 1: that gives
       session 1 three cuts plus setup against session 2's two, which is E113. Name
       a drop candidate inside session 2 instead. For Gate 3.
  W6 (test-runner), W7 (deploy-check) - owned downstream, no action here.

The suite was read as part of this gate, not just the plan: 11 tests, one per criterion, each recording which ambiguity reading it took in its docstring. Red-first ran static-only - correct with no app/ on disk, since a dynamic all-red run would pass for the wrong reason. The dynamic proof is the step-10 skeleton check.

gate2.note:
GATE 2 APPROVED. Human decision. Read as every criterion, not as a summary.

RESULTS: 11 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip, 0 missing. pytest rc 0, 11 passed in 8.37s. Session 1 c-1-1..c-1-5 and session 2 c-2-1..c-2-6 all green. Built first time - code retries 0/15, no builder/test-runner loop. code_checks declared none, so none run.

MUTATION: 5 of 5 tasks checked, 0 ungraded, 0 inconclusive. For every cut the set that went red equals the set that grades it, with stayed_green empty in all five:
  cut-runs-of      18 lines -> c-1-1 c-1-2 c-1-3 c-1-4 c-2-1 c-2-2 c-2-3
  cut-line-status  18 lines -> c-2-1 c-2-2 c-2-3 c-2-6
  cut-transpose    11 lines -> c-1-2 c-1-4 c-2-1 c-2-3 c-2-6
  cut-cell-cycle   13 lines -> c-2-5 c-2-6
  cut-board-solved  8 lines -> c-2-1 c-2-6
No student task is ungraded and none is graded by a criterion that does not name it.

RULE 3 SHOWN, NOT ASSERTED: git reports verify/ byte-identical to the Gate 1 commit 8499e26 - the suite that graded this code is the one approved before any code existed. spec-status drift null, still frozen at 729cfc0b1ba5, so the Builder edited neither the tests nor the spec.

THE TWO GATE 1 WATCH ITEMS, CHECKED BY HAND RATHER THAN BY TEST:
  W4 CLEAR - lib/puzzles.ts puzzleFor returns an object literal with exactly id,
       title, size, rowClues, colClues. No spread, and the Puzzle type admits
       nothing else. solutionRows is separate and server-side only; the solution
       never enters the response. The spec's stricter 'no other key' prose holds
       even though c-1-1 grades only 'no solution key'.
  W1 RESOLVED THE SAFE WAY - Board.tsx documents the reading taken ('a clue keeps
       the status it is already showing until a response is applied') and
       sendCheck enforces it with a sequence guard: setResult fires only when
       seq === sent.current, so a stale answer is dropped and nothing repaints in
       the gap between a click and its response. No blink. This also implements
       W2's ungraded out-of-order discard rule.

Marker placement, which was round 2's blocker, is as the round-3 spec pinned it: handleCellClick keeps 'let updated = grid' above the marker and setGrid / sendCheck below it.

STILL OPEN FOR GATE 3: W5 - session 2 budgeted to exactly 40 with no slack while carrying the largest cut. Do NOT fix by moving a cut into session 1 (E113); name a drop candidate inside session 2. W3 - board-loading and the text of puzzle-title remain declared and ungraded.

gate3.note:
GATE 3 APPROVED. Human decision, made with the timing overrun in front of it.

THE GATE'S QUESTION IS ANSWERED YES: the step 13 dry run on 2026-08-29 recorded taught_without_the_code true - Priya, who did not build it, taught session 2 from the guide alone without opening app/, and students implemented the project. That is what Gate 3 asks and it is answered with evidence rather than opinion.

HANDOVER CHECKS ALL GREEN: leak scan clean - 28 answer lines watched across 5 tasks, 0 leaks in the student tree and 0 in its history. skeleton-check 11 checked, 0 mismatches, 0 partial-state risks, typecheck_fail_open false. guide-lint 0 errors / 0 warnings over 4 files, session 2 disclosed true. deploy ok - fresh copy, install 58 packages, next build compiled in 18.3s, 0 advisories. Cut ran first pass, 5 cuts, 0 retries. Checked by hand: every return in lib/nonogram.ts sits below its cut so the skeleton compiles, and SEEDS survives in skeleton/lib/puzzles.ts because the server derives from it while no derivation ships.

ACCEPTED WITH EYES OPEN - THE TIMING. stack.json budgets 40 minutes a session. The pack-writer's honest estimate for session 2 was 48 and disclosed it at the top of session-2.md. Priya measured 50. That is 25 percent over budget and 2 past an estimate already flagged as uncomfortable. It is not known from the dry-run note whether the two marked levers (pre-write the four lineStatus const lines at minute 12; walk cut-board-solved rather than type it at minute 25) were pulled - if they were not, session 2 may still land near 40 when they are; if they were, the 40-minute plan table does not hold and cut-line-status needs splitting.

SHIPPING ANYWAY IS THE DECISION: teachability is the bar Gate 3 sets, and it was cleared. An instructor running session 2 should expect 50 minutes, not 40, and should be told so before they schedule it.

THIS IS THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE PROJECT TO OVERRUN ON THE SAME SHAPE - one cut much larger than its siblings, most recently habit-tracker's cut-api-toggle at 6 estimated against roughly 20 measured. learning/lessons.md should record that a spec-linter minute budget is not evidence and that the pattern now has four data points; the fix belongs upstream in the spec, capping a single cut's share of a session, not in the pack. Update it between runs, never during one.

STILL UNGRADED AND SHIPPING: W1 (what a clue strip shows between a click and its response - the shipped sequence counter in sendCheck resolves it safely but no criterion observes it), W2 (the out-of-order discard rule), W3 (board-loading and the text of puzzle-title). All non-blocking, all recorded at Gate 1.
